raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

`VLLM_PLUGINS` matches plugin names against the entry point registry by exact string, so a name that matches nothing is dropped silently — no error, no warning, exit code 0. `docs/design/lora_resolver_plugins.md:13` names the built-in HF Hub resolver `hf_hub_resolver`, but `pyproject.toml:47` registers it as `lora_hf_hub_resolver`. Following the doc loads nothing: the resolver is never registered, and requests fail later with "adapter not found".

Fixing the doc alone is not enough. The wrong name has shipped in released docs (e.g. v0.25.0) and in configs the project does not control; and the existing guard in `hf_hub_resolver.py` cannot cover this case, because it is the entry point target and only runs once the plugin is loaded — which already requires the name to match.

This warns once per process when a `VLLM_PLUGINS` name matches no installed plugin, and lists the available names.

## Claims

- An unknown `VLLM_PLUGINS` name now emits a warning listing the available plugin names, instead of being ignored with no diagnostics.
- `docs/design/lora_resolver_plugins.md:13` now uses `lora_hf_hub_resolver`.
- No model output, accuracy, or serving behaviour changes, so no model evaluation is included.

## Validation

`load_general_plugins()` returns `None`, so the reproducer observes the log rather than a return value.

    # before (main) / after (this branch): the typo is silent on main, warned here
    VLLM_PLUGINS=hf_hub_resolver python -c "from vllm.plugins import load_general_plugins; load_general_plugins()"
    main:  (no output — a typo is indistinguishable from a correct name)
    here:  VLLM_PLUGINS contains ['hf_hub_resolver'], which match no installed plugin. These entries will be ignored. Available plugins: ['lora_filesystem_resolver', 'lora_hf_hub_resolver']

    # a valid name must not warn (guards the cross-group union against false positives)
    VLLM_PLUGINS=lora_hf_hub_resolver python -c "from vllm.plugins import load_general_plugins; load_general_plugins()"
    (no output)

    # with the documented name the resolver is never registered
    VLLM_LORA_RESOLVER_HF_REPO_LIST=foo/bar VLLM_PLUGINS=hf_hub_resolver python - <<'EOF'
    from vllm.plugins import load_general_plugins
    from vllm.lora.resolver import LoRAResolverRegistry
    load_general_plugins()
    print(sorted(LoRAResolverRegistry.get_supported_resolvers()))
    EOF
    []

    # real server, single GPU (vLLM 0.31.1rc1.dev245+gbe0823357): warning once per process at startup, before the model loads
    VLLM_PLUGINS=hf_hub_resolver vllm serve Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct --enable-lora --gpu-memory-utilization 0.8
    (EngineCore pid=6295) WARNING ... [__init__.py:104] VLLM_PLUGINS contains ['hf_hub_resolver'], which match no installed plugin. These entries will be ignored. Available plugins: ['lora_filesystem_resolver', 'lora_hf_hub_resolver']

Lint: `pre-commit run --files vllm/plugins/__init__.py docs/design/lora_resolver_plugins.md` — all hooks passed.

## Details

Root cause: `vllm/envs.py` parses `VLLM_PLUGINS` with `.split(",")`, and `load_plugins_by_group` tests `plugin.name in allowed_plugins` — exact membership; an unmatched name is dropped with no signal.

`VLLM_PLUGINS` is one global allowlist shared by all five plugin groups, so "unknown" is judged against the union of every group's entry points; a per-group check would false-positive on another group's names. The check lives in `load_general_plugins` rather than `load_plugins_by_group` because it does not use the `group` argument and can reuse the existing once-per-process `plugins_loaded` guard, adding no new module-level state.

It is informational, not a failure: it names both the unmatched entries and the available names, so an intentional absence (e.g. one `VLLM_PLUGINS` shared across heterogeneous containers) is recognisable rather than alarming. It only fires when `VLLM_PLUGINS` is set and lists a name not installed anywhere in this environment; unset, or `VLLM_PLUGINS=""` (which parses to `[""]` and is excluded), stays silent.

The available names are already logged, but only at `DEBUG` for this group, and that log never says a `VLLM_PLUGINS` entry matched nothing — searching it for the typo'd name even hits the module path, which reads as "it's there".

No new test is added: per `pr-checklist` §2 a bugfix is validated on a reproducer, and §2.1 discourages unnecessary tests.

**Duplicate check**: searched `gh pr list` / `gh issue list` for `"hf_hub_resolver"`, `"lora resolver docs"`, `"VLLM_PLUGINS plugin name"` and `"lora_resolver_plugins"` — nothing addresses unmatched `VLLM_PLUGINS` names. #54428 ("Don't fail the request when a LoRA resolver raises") is runtime error handling in `serving.py` / `filesystem_resolver.py`, no file overlap.

**AI assistance**: drafted with AI assistance (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash); the human submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the commands above.

nodes.body:
Hi @hmellor! This is a small bugfix for `VLLM_PLUGINS` — small, but easy to miss: an unknown name is matched by exact entry point name and silently dropped, so a misconfigured allowlist disables a plugin with no error or warning (that is how `hf_hub_resolver` vs `lora_hf_hub_resolver` went unnoticed). This adds a once-per-process warning naming the unmatched entries and the available plugins, and fixes the doc line that documented the wrong name. Details and the before/after reproducer are in the PR description. Could you take a look when you have a moment? Thanks!

If you have any other suggestions or requests, I'm happy to make further changes as well.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

files.patch:
@@ -10,7 +10,7 @@ receives a request for a LoRA adapter that hasn't been loaded yet, the resolver
 to locate and load the adapter from their configured storage locations. This enables:
 
 - **Dynamic LoRA Loading**: Load adapters on-demand without server restarts
-- **Multiple Storage Backends**: Support for filesystem, S3, and custom backends. The built-in `lora_filesystem_resolver` requires a local storage path, while the built-in `hf_hub_resolver` will pull LoRA adapters from Huggingface Hub and proceed in an identical manner. In general, custom resolvers can be implemented to fetch from any source.
+- **Multiple Storage Backends**: Support for filesystem, S3, and custom backends. The built-in `lora_filesystem_resolver` requires a local storage path, while the built-in `lora_hf_hub_resolver` will pull LoRA adapters from Huggingface Hub and proceed in an identical manner. In general, custom resolvers can be implemented to fetch from any source.
 - **Automatic Discovery**: Seamless integration with existing LoRA workflows
 - **Scalable Deployment**: Centralized adapter management across multiple vLLM instances

@@ -84,6 +84,30 @@ def load_general_plugins():
         return
     plugins_loaded = True
 
+    allowed_plugins = envs.VLLM_PLUGINS
+    if allowed_plugins is not None:
+        from importlib.metadata import entry_points
+
+        available_plugins = {
+            p.name
+            for group in (
+                DEFAULT_PLUGINS_GROUP,
+                IO_PROCESSOR_PLUGINS_GROUP,
+                PLATFORM_PLUGINS_GROUP,
+                STAT_LOGGER_PLUGINS_GROUP,
+                ENDPOINT_PLUGINS_GROUP,
+            )
+            for p in entry_points(group=group)
+        }
+        unknown = sorted(set(allowed_plugins) - available_plugins - {""})
+        if unknown:
+            logger.warning(
+                "VLLM_PLUGINS contains %s, which match no installed plugin. "
+                "These entries will be ignored. Available plugins: %s",
+                unknown,
+                sorted(available_plugins),
+            )
+
     plugins = load_plugins_by_group(group=DEFAULT_PLUGINS_GROUP)
     # general plugins, we only need to execute the loaded functions
     for func in plugins.values():
